## Research Dossier: Issue 065 (2026-09-17)

This dossier contains verified cultural signals compiled within the past 24 hours (with expanded search windows up to 14 days where specified) mapped directly to Muki’s core research interests: feminist visual culture, photographic archives, East Asian image history, and AI-native creative technologies.

---

### Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal

* **Proposed Headline**: 罗马 MACRO 举办 Marialba Russo 回顾展：以“反转之视”重构 1970 年代先锋摄影与女性主义视线
* **Original English Title**: Sguardo rovescio: Marialba Russo’s First Major Museum Retrospective at MACRO, Rome
* **English Summary**: MACRO in Rome is launching “Sguardo rovescio” (Reverse Gaze), the first major museum retrospective dedicated to Italian photographer Marialba Russo, showcasing her pioneering 1970s bodies of work that challenge the patriarchal gaze.
* **Specific Source URL**: `https://www.meer.com/en/81223-marialba-russo-sguardo-rovescio`
* **Publication Date**: September 15, 2026
* **Proposed Section**: Feminist Structure Signal
* **Duplication Assessment**: `New` (Marialba Russo and this retrospective have not appeared in recent-issue contexts).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * **What happened**: The Museo d'Arte Contemporanea di Roma (MACRO) is opening the autumn exhibition season on September 24, 2026, with the retrospective "Sguardo rovescio," dedicated to Italian photographer Marialba Russo (b. 1947). The exhibition runs until January 31, 2027.
  * **Curators**: Cristiana Perrella and Elena Magini.
  * **Core Materials**: The exhibition brings together seven core series from Russo's 1970s production: *Al ristorante, il 29 settembre 1974* (1974); *Travestimento* (1975–80); *Il passaggio – l'incanata* (1979); *Il parto* (1978); *Della serie delle centotrenta figure di spalle* (1981); *Cult fiction* (1978–80); and *L'espulsione del male* (1974).
  * **Thematic Scope**: The title "Sguardo rovescio" (Reverse Gaze) directly refers to the reversal of the canonical viewpoint in deeply patriarchal 1970s Italy. It dialogues directly with Laura Mulvey’s concept of the "male gaze," using a female lens to scrutinize and isolate masculinity as a cultural construct rather than a natural given, capturing men who surrender themselves to rituals or discard virile stereotypes.
* **Muki Relevance**: 
  This retrospective offers a highly rigorous visual anthropology and feminist critique methodology. Russo’s active inversion of the "male gaze" is not a simplistic visual opposition, but a structural deconstruction of societal rituals, drag, labor, and bodily politics in southern Italy. It serves as an essential primary source for researching 1970s Mediterranean feminist art history and counter-archiving.

### Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal (Photographic Archive)

* **Proposed Headline**: The 8th Floor 举办 Carlos Martiel 个展《Dark Age》：以肉身极限与推测性档案探讨权力的形而上学
* **Original English Title**: Carlos Martiel: Dark Age Solo Exhibition at The 8th Floor, New York
* **English Summary**: The Shelley & Donald Rubin Foundation presents “Dark Age,” a solo exhibition by Cuban performance artist Carlos Martiel, exploring the temporality of performance, physical endurance, and bodily archives through live actions and drawings.
* **Specific Source URL**: `https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/811802/carlos-martiel-dark-age/`
* **Publication Date**: September 3, 2026 (Exhibition opens September 17, 2026)
* **Proposed Section**: Visual Culture Signal
* **Duplication Assessment**: `New` (Carlos Martiel’s upcoming solo project has not been covered).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * **What happened**: The Shelley & Donald Rubin Foundation is presenting *Dark Age*, a solo exhibition of Cuban performance artist Carlos Martiel, opening September 17, 2026, at The 8th Floor, New York (on view through January 30, 2027).
  * **Performances & Work**: Martiel will perform three new live actions: *Dark Age* (September 19), *Mano de hierro (Iron Hand)* (October 8), and *Fear of Them (Miedo a ellos)* (December 10). The exhibition will feature documentation, drawings, and ephemera from his past works.
  * **Key details**: The project addresses performance temporality and how to make ephemeral live actions structural. It transitions from solo bodily performances (such as *Lazos de Sangre*, 2010) to family participation, featuring his brother in the title piece. Additionally, it debuts his drawing suite *Metafísica del poder* (Metaphysics of power).
  * **Artist quote**: Martiel states, "My body is an archive of my performances; the scars I have drawn on it reveal the battlefield...".
* **Muki Relevance**: 
  The exhibition serves as a critical study of "body as archive" (身体即档案) and "bodily duration." Martiel’s extreme physical endurances and self-inflicted marks act as visceral counter-narratives to colonial and institutional violence. It directly relates to research on the curation of ephemeral art, body politics, and structural institutional critique.

### Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal

* **Proposed Headline**: 徕卡画廊中国大陆首馆落户上海西岸：开馆大展“马克·吕布：中国记忆”回顾半个世纪的城市与社会变迁
* **Original English Title**: Memories of China: The Inauguration of Leica Gallery Shanghai Westbund Central with Marc Riboud’s Retrospective
* **English Summary**: Leica Gallery Shanghai Westbund Central, Leica's first brand-owned gallery on the Chinese mainland, has opened with a major retrospective dedicated to French photographer Marc Riboud, showcasing 30 original prints from his five-decade journey in China.
* **Specific Source URL**: `https://leica-camera.com/en-US/event/leica-gallery-shanghai-westbund-central/memories-china-marc-riboud` (Alternate verification page: `https://leica-camera.com/sites/default/files/` and `https://www.lfi-online.de`)
* **Publication Date**: September 12, 2026 (Official opening announcement; Westbund Central press release updated September 17, 2026).
* **Proposed Section**: China / East Asia Signal
* **Duplication Assessment**: `New` (First mainland brand-owned Leica gallery opening and this specific exhibition are entirely new).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * **What happened**: Leica Gallery Shanghai Westbund Central, Leica's first brand-owned gallery on the Chinese Mainland, officially opened in the Westbund art district of Shanghai (Shop B-L1-16, No. 858-5 Damuqiao Road, Xuhui District). 
  * **Inaugural Exhibition**: The space opens with *Memories of China* by Marc Riboud (September 12 – December 3, 2026).
  * **Exhibition Scope**: The show presents 30 original works by the legendary French photographer spanning over five decades, capturing China’s transformation from his initial visit in 1957 to the economic boom of the 2000s. It includes historic masterpieces like *The Painter on the Eiffel Tower* and *Antique shopwindow in Liulichang*, alongside raw humanistic street scenes.
* **Muki Relevance**: 
  The entry of Leica's first corporate brand-owned gallery on the Chinese mainland marks a notable institutional shift in how photographic archives and visual legacies are curated, presented, and funded in Shanghai's flagship art district (Westbund). The dual focus on Marc Riboud's historic archives offers a valuable case study in the intersection of corporate branding, public diplomacy, and Chinese social-historical image indexing.

### Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Proposed Headline**: 开放音频音乐大模型 YuE2-3B 发布：引入可编辑乐谱图层实现白盒化与智能体协同创作
* **Original English Title**: YuE2-3B: Open-Source Music Generation with Editable Scores from Multimodal Art Projection
* **English Summary**: Multimodal Art Projection has released YuE2-3B, a 3-billion-parameter open-weights music model that introduces an editable symbolic planning score in ABC notation, enabling composers and agents to co-edit composition structures before rendering.
* **Specific Source URL**: `https://huggingface.co/m-a-p/YuE2-3B` (Alternate: Github `https://github.com/multimodal-art-projection/YuE`)
* **Publication Date**: September 9, 2026
* **Proposed Section**: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
* **Duplication Assessment**: `New` (YuE2-3B is a newly released model and represents a distinct architectural development from its predecessor, YuE).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * **What happened**: The Multimodal Art Projection (m-a-p) research team (spanning HKUST, Tokenwave.AI, NYU, Stanford, etc.) open-sourced YuE2-3B, a 3-billion-parameter music generation model. 
  * **Performance Metrics**: On 192 WildSongBench prompts, YuE2 (with best-of-8 sampling) scored a SongBench average of 6.9632, outperforming proprietary systems like Suno v5 (6.8721).
  * **Technical Innovation**: YuE2 introduces "symbolic planning with an editable score." Instead of rendering straight from text to raw audio, YuE2 first writes a symbolic plan in ABC notation (detailing melody and chords). 
  * **Workflow Capabilities**: Users can input, revise, and customize the score directly. This enables: (1) precise score-level editing; (2) zero-shot covers by transcribing existing audio using SheetSage2 and re-rendering it in a new style; and (3) agentic music editing, where natural language feedback is translated by an LLM agent into score edits for iterative rendering.
  * **Ecosystem updates**: ComfyUI added native support for YuE2 on its `yue2` branch (PR #16250), and a community developer released the missing `realaudio-tokenizer-v4` to encode real audio into YuE2 tokens on September 14, 2026.
* **Muki Relevance**: 
  YuE2 represents a crucial workflow shift from black-box "prompt-and-pray" text-to-audio generation to white-box symbolic control. By establishing an editable midi/score-like intermediate layer, it allows human creators and AI agents to work together programmatically. This serves as a vital signal for Muki’s interest in agent-native workflows, technological co-authorship, and procedural music archeology.

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Proposed Headline**: 第十届 PhMuseum 女性摄影师资助计划启动：提供万元奖金与博洛尼亚个展机会
* **Original English Title**: 10th Edition of the PhMuseum Women Photographers Grant Open for Submissions
* **English Summary**: The 10th annual PhMuseum Women Photographers Grant is accepting submissions until its October 15 deadline (early bird September 24), offering €10,000 in cash prizes, solo exhibitions, and screenings at the PhotoVogue Festival to support female and non-binary artists.
* **Specific Source URL**: `https://phmuseum.com/grants/women-photographers-grant-2026`
* **Publication Date**: September 8, 2026 (Open call launched; Early bird deadline September 24, 2026, final deadline October 15, 2026).
* **Proposed Section**: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
* **Duplication Assessment**: `New` (This is the newly opened 2026 edition of the grant; different from previous years’ archives).
* **Verified Facts**:
  * **What happened**: The PhMuseum Women Photographers Grant has launched its 10th edition. 
  * **Eligibility**: Open to female and non-binary professional and emerging photographers worldwide.
  * **Prizes**: A total of €10,000 in cash prizes will be awarded (First place: €5,000; Second place: €2,000; Third place: €1,000; New Generation category: €2,000). Additional prizes include: two €2,500 vouchers from equipment partner MPB; a solo exhibition at PhMuseum Lab in Bologna in June 2027 (with travel and production covered); up to 40 shortlisted works screened at the PhotoVogue Festival 2027 in Milan; and 1-on-1 online portfolio reviews.
  * **Application requirements**: Submission of a project consisting of 5 to 20 photos centered on a specific theme, narrative, or concept. Early bird deadline is September 24, 2026 ($35 fee); the final deadline is October 15, 2026 ($40 fee).
  * **Jurors**: Elisa Medde (Editor/Curator), Mariela Sancari (Photographer), Yagazie Emezi (Artist), and Myriam Boulos (Photographer).
* **Muki Relevance**: 
  This is a highly structured, prestigious funding opportunity directly supporting Muki’s communities of practice (women and non-binary lens-based workers). The inclusion of a solo museum-quality exhibition and integration with the PhotoVogue network provides an immediate career-advancing platform. It remains a crucial lead for independent curation and lens-based care research.

Introducing the Sept 16 curator's guide would represent a near-duplicate topic without a sufficiently distinct structural development.
* **Apple's "What Holds Us" Exhibition (September 16, 2026)**: Curated by Kathy Ryan on iPhone 18 Pro. While relevant to general mobile photography trends, this represents a highly commercialized marketing push by Apple rather than an independent artistic or feminist visual culture signal.
* **ComfyUI v0.35.2 / FastH3 local serving updates**: While important, Muki's recent issues (`2026-09-15` and `2026-09-16`) extensively tracked ComfyUI core updates, agent frameworks, and H3 performance. Selecting the open-source release of **YuE2-3B** instead serves as a stronger, fresher paradigm shift in agentic multimodal composition rather than a repetitive local CUDA/performance update.
